title: Boiler Feedwater Pump

introduction.definition: A boiler feedwater pump delivers hot water from the deaerator to the boiler or steam generator at a pressure above drum pressure. It is a horizontal multistage centrifugal pump — ring-section (BB4) or barrel (BB5) — with a balance device for axial thrust and a minimum-flow line to protect it at low boiler demand.
applications: Alumina refinery steam and power plants
key_points: Hot, near-saturated suction — NPSH critical (booster pump or elevated deaerator)
Speed control by VFD, fluid coupling or turbine drive on large units

classification.configuration: Horizontal, between bearings, ring-section (segmental), radially split
classification.api_610_type: BB4 (single casing, radially split, multistage); barrel BB5 for highest pressures

introduction.summary: A boiler feedwater pump raises water from the deaerator (low pressure, near saturation temperature) to above boiler drum or steam-generator pressure — often well over 100 bar in power plants. To reach that head at reasonable speed it uses several impellers in series: after each impeller a diffuser recovers pressure and return vanes lead the water inward to the next impeller eye. The stage casings are clamped between suction and discharge casings by tie bolts (ring-section design). A balance drum at the high-pressure end cancels most of the axial thrust. A minimum-flow recirculation valve protects the pump at low boiler demand.

pressure.title: Stage-by-stage pressure
pressure.description: Colour rings show static pressure rising from suction (blue) to discharge (red). Each stage adds roughly the same head, so total head ≈ number of stages × head per stage at the same flow.

thrust.title: Axial thrust & balancing
thrust.description: Each impeller is pushed towards suction (magenta) because its back shroud sees higher pressure than the eye side. The balance drum (green) has full discharge pressure on its inner face and near-suction pressure in the balance chamber behind it (leak-off line), creating an opposing force. A thrust bearing carries the small residual.

foundation: Rigid foundation; thermal growth allowance; centreline-supported casings for hot service.
alignment: Align pump and motor shafts with dial indicators or laser after grouting and again after connecting the piping (hot alignment check for hot service).
Target the coupling manufacturer's tolerances; typical practice for 1500–3000 rpm is ≤0.05 mm offset and ≤0.05 mm/100 mm angularity — verify.
Correct soft foot (< 0.05 mm) before final alignment.
piping: Booster pump or sufficient deaerator elevation for NPSHa.
Automatic recirculation (minimum flow) valve on discharge.
commissioning: Warm up the casing evenly before start.
Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Start against a partly open discharge valve, then open to the duty point; avoid running at shut-off.
Record baseline vibration, bearing temperature, suction and discharge pressure, flow and motor current.

routine.task: Monitor balance leak-off and thrust bearing.

overhaul.task: Inspect first-stage impeller for cavitation; measure clearances.

script.narration: This module introduces the Boiler Feedwater Pump.
A boiler feedwater pump delivers hot water from the deaerator to the boiler or steam generator at a pressure above drum pressure.
It is a horizontal multistage centrifugal pump — ring-section (BB4) or barrel (BB5) — with a balance device for axial thrust and a minimum-flow line to protect it at low boiler demand.
Typical applications include utility and industrial power plants; cogeneration and process steam boilers; alumina refinery steam and power plants; heat-recovery steam generators (HRSG).

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Boiler Feedwater Pump.
Monitor balance leak-off and thrust bearing.
Check recirculation valve operation.
Inspect first-stage impeller for cavitation; measure clearances.
Watch for cavitation at first stage: noise, pitting. Common cause: deaerator level/pressure transients.
Watch for thermal shock: rubbing, seizure. Common cause: cold start on hot water.
Watch for balance device wear: leak-off rise. Common cause: erosion.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
